name: Litpal
subcategory: academic research and literature review assistant
tagline: AI assistant for reading papers, running literature searches, and drafting academic writing with citations.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The chat-over-your-PDFs part is a solved weekend project: parse, chunk, embed, retrieve, answer with page citations. What you cannot casually rebuild is the literature discovery layer, because that depends on access to indexed paper metadata and full text at scale. You can get surprisingly far on free scholarly APIs like OpenAlex, Crossref, arXiv, and Semantic Scholar, but coverage is patchy and paywalled publisher text is simply not yours to fetch. So a personal version is genuinely useful for the papers you already have, and mediocre at telling you which papers you should have. Budget for API token costs and expect the citation formatting to be less clean than a product that has been tuned on it.
coreLoopDIY: A local app that ingests your PDF library, indexes it into a vector store, answers questions with page-level citations, and searches OpenAlex and arXiv for related work.
requirements: Python 3.11 plus Node for the frontend
Local disk for PDFs and a SQLite or LanceDB index
Willingness to hit free scholarly APIs with polite rate limits
whatYouLose: Broad indexed coverage of paywalled journal literature
Tuned citation extraction and reference formatting that mostly just works
Hosted sync so your library follows you across devices
Ongoing model and prompt improvements you do not have to maintain
Collaboration and sharing of annotated papers with co-authors
moatNotes: The moat is less the model and more the pipeline that turns messy publisher PDFs and metadata into reliable, citable text.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the failure mode of a homemade research assistant is a confident wrong citation, and in academic writing that costs more than a subscription. Paying products invest heavily in the boring parts: reference parsing, dedup across preprint and published versions, page-accurate quoting, export to BibTeX and Word. Also, most researchers do not want to babysit an embedding pipeline at 11pm before a deadline. If your library is small and your standards for retrieval are your own, the DIY version is fine.
notes: Great at your own PDFs, weak at finding the ones you have not downloaded yet.
prompt:
Build a local-first academic reading and literature assistant. No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Backend: Python 3.11, FastAPI, uvicorn.
- PDF parsing: pymupdf, keeping page numbers per text block.
- Embeddings and chat: OpenAI API, key from .env as OPENAI_API_KEY.
- Vector store: LanceDB on local disk under ./data/index.
- Metadata: SQLite via sqlite3, file ./data/litpal.db.
- Frontend: Vite plus React plus TypeScript, plain CSS, no UI kit.

Features in scope:
1. Drop PDFs into ./papers or upload through the UI. A watcher ingests new files: extract text per page, chunk to roughly 1200 characters with 150 overlap, embed, store chunk text plus file plus page.
2. Metadata guessing: try DOI regex in the first two pages, then look it up on Crossref to fill title, authors, year, journal. Fall back to filename.
3. Ask panel: question goes to top-k retrieval across the whole library or a filtered subset, answer streams back with inline markers like [3] mapping to file and page. Clicking a marker opens the PDF at that page.
4. Per-paper summary: one click produces structured notes covering research question, method, findings, limitations.
5. Discovery: search OpenAlex and arXiv by keyword or by a seed paper's DOI, show title, year, abstract, citation count, open access PDF link when present. One-click download into ./papers.
6. Export: BibTeX for any selected papers, and markdown export of notes and answers with citations.

Out of scope, do not build: user auth, multi-user, payments, mobile app, scraping paywalled publisher sites, Word add-ins, real-time collaboration.

Rules:
- Never fabricate a citation. If retrieval returns nothing above the score threshold, say so and answer nothing.
- Cache all external API responses to disk. Send a descriptive User-Agent with contact email from .env and respect rate limits.
- Ship .env.example, a README with setup in under ten commands, and a seed script that ingests two sample arXiv PDFs so the app is not empty on first run.
